## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dutiyaujjagghika* is the twelfth training rule of the Sekhiya section of the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga in the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. It establishes monastic etiquette concerning loud laughter while in inhabited areas. The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 Within the Pali canon, it corresponds to Bhikkhu Pātimokkha Sekhiya 12, Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga and Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha Sekhiya 12, and the corresponding rules in the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Parivāra. Across non-Theravāda lineages, parallels survive in Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan traditions, including the Sarvāstivāda Pātimokkha, the Mahīśāsaka Vinaya and Pātimokkha traditions for monks and nuns, the Dharmaguptaka Vinaya and Pātimokkha texts, the Mahāsāṅghika and Lokottaravāda Vinayas and Pātimokkhas, and the *Upāliparipṛcchā*.
